reports_target_markers.evidence: The paper reports genotyping of the Vgsc L1014F (kdr-west) marker.

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: Table 2 provides the number of mosquitoes genotyped (N) and the number/frequency of the kdr L1014F mutation for each site.

african_field_population.evidence: The mosquitoes were collected from ten urban sites in eastern Ethiopia.

is_primary_study.evidence: This is an empirical study analyzing field-collected mosquito samples.

sub_country_location.evidence: The paper provides data for ten specific urban sites (e.g., Awash Sebat Kilo, Bati, Dire Dawa, etc.).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: The collection period is stated as August to November 2018.

duplicate_risk.evidence: The paper states that the DNA samples were extracted from mosquitoes collected in a previous study (Balkew et al., 2020), but this paper presents new molecular analysis (kdr genotyping) on those samples.

supplement.evidence: All necessary data, including genotype counts and frequencies, are provided in the main text and tables.

assessment.summary: This study analyzed the kdr L1014F mutation in 159 Anopheles stephensi mosquitoes collected from ten sites in eastern Ethiopia in 2018. The mutation was found at a low frequency (5.7%), and no association was found between the kdr mutation and permethrin resistance in a subset of 40 mosquitoes from Dire Dawa.
